title: Google Calendar Cuts Off Event Titles When Printing? How to Print the Full Details
excerpt: Google Calendar's print page cuts long titles and drops descriptions in Week and Month view. What you can fix in the built-in settings, the Schedule view trick, and how to print the full grid.
content:
Short answer: Google Calendar's print page squeezes each event into the grid, so long titles get cut and descriptions never appear in Week or Month view. Inside Google Calendar you can only reduce the damage: use a smaller font, landscape paper, fewer days, or switch to Schedule view with Print descriptions turned on. If you need full titles, descriptions and locations inside a week or month grid, use a print add-on such as Daywrap (made by us).

Written: November 2026, Google Calendar on the web.

Why the text gets cut off

The print page draws the same grid you see on screen. Each event gets a fixed slot, and anything that does not fit is cut at the edge of that slot. Short events on a busy day are hit hardest: a 30-minute meeting gets one line, so "Quarterly budget review with finance team" turns into "Quarterly bud…". The Week and Month grids also have no option for descriptions or locations; only Schedule view can print descriptions.

Which situation are you in?

  • A few titles are cut, and you only need titles: try the settings in Method 1 first.
  • You need descriptions or locations on paper, and a list is fine: use Schedule view (Method 2).
  • You need a week or month grid with nothing cut: Method 3.

Compare the ways

Way Full titles Descriptions and locations Grid layout Cost
Smaller font, landscape (built-in) Better, not guaranteed No Yes Free
Schedule view + Print descriptions (built-in) Yes Descriptions No, a list Free
Daywrap add-on (ours) Yes, titles wrap Yes Yes (month, week or list) Free; paid $15 one-time

Method 1: Make more room in the built-in print page

  1. Open Google Calendar on a computer and pick Week (or Month) at the top right.
  2. Click Settings (gear icon) → Print.
  3. In Print preview, set Font size to the smallest size and Orientation to Landscape.
  4. If you only need part of the week, pick a shorter custom range first, so each day gets a wider column.

This helps with titles that are a little too long. It does not add descriptions, and very short events can still be cut.

Method 2: Print a list with Schedule view

  1. Switch the view at the top right to Schedule.
  2. Click Settings → Print and turn on Print descriptions.
  3. Click Print (choose Save as PDF as the destination for a PDF).

You get every event with its full title and description, but as a list by date instead of a calendar grid.

Method 3: Print the grid with full titles and descriptions (add-on)

Daywrap for Google Calendar is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It prints your month, week or a day-by-day list on one page, with every title in full (wrapped instead of cut) and the description and location under each event. Busy days get more room and quiet days less, and the text size adjusts to the paper.

  1. Install Daywrap from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Open Google Calendar and click the Daywrap icon in the side panel.
  3. Click Open print page and allow read-only access.
  4. Choose month, week or list, the calendar, the paper (Letter, A4, Legal or A3) and the orientation, then click Print / Save as PDF.

Daywrap only reads your events; it cannot create, change or delete anything, and your events are not sent to our servers. The free version has no watermark and prints one calendar at a time. The paid version (a one-time $15) adds several calendars on one print, up to 12 months in one go, a Monday or Saturday week start, and options to show or hide end times, weekends and week numbers. Details are on the Daywrap product page.

Pitfalls

  • Declined events take up space. Hide them in the print settings (both the built-in page and Daywrap can do this).
  • Phone app: the Google Calendar app has no print page. Print from a computer.
  • Long descriptions with links: the built-in Schedule print keeps them as they are; Daywrap turns links and formatting into plain text so they fit.

FAQ

Can I print Google Calendar week view with descriptions without an add-on? Not in the week grid. Use Schedule view with Print descriptions, which prints a list.

Why does month view show "+3 more" instead of the events? A month grid has limited space per day. Landscape and a small font help; an add-on that gives busy days more room helps more.

Can I save it as a PDF instead of printing? Yes. In the print dialog, change the destination to Save as PDF.

For every built-in print option, see our step-by-step guide: Print Google Calendar: Week and Month View.

title: How to Put 2, 4 or 6 Photos on One Slide in Google Slides (Photo Grid)
excerpt: Google Slides has no photo grid or collage layout. Make a 2, 4 or 6 photo grid by hand with crop, Align and Distribute, or build many grid slides at once with an add-on.
alt: Photo Slides sidebar with 4 photos per slide and date captions
content:
Short answer: Google Slides has no photo grid or collage layout. To put 2, 4 or 6 photos on one slide, insert them, crop them to the same shape, and line them up with Arrange → Align and Arrange → Distribute. That is fine for one or two slides. For a whole album in a grid, an add-on such as Photo Slides (made by us) builds the grid slides for you.

Written: November 2026, Google Slides in Chrome.

Which situation are you in?

  • One or two slides with a few photos: do it by hand (Method 1).
  • Dozens of photos, a few per slide (a trip, an event, a class project): Method 2 saves the most time.
  • One photo per slide instead: see One Photo Per Slide in Google Slides.

Compare the ways

Way Photos per slide Good for Cost
Insert, crop and align by hand Any A few slides Free
Photo Slides add-on (ours) 1, 2, 4 or 6 Many photos at once Free for 1 per slide (20 at a time); grids are in the paid version, $19 one-time

Method 1: Make a grid by hand

  1. Go to Insert → Image → Upload from computer and select the photos for this slide. They all land on the current slide, stacked on top of each other.
  2. Resize one photo to the size you want for each cell of the grid.
  3. To make every photo the same shape, double-click a photo to crop it, or use the arrow next to the crop button to mask it to a shape.
  4. Turn on View → Guides → Show guides if you want to drag guides to the cell edges.
  5. Drag the photos roughly into rows. Then select a row and use Arrange → Align → Middle, and Arrange → Distribute → Horizontally to space them evenly. Do the same for columns with Align → Center and Distribute → Vertically.
  6. For captions, add a text box under each photo.

Once one slide looks right, duplicate it (Slide → Duplicate slide) and replace the photos: right-click a photo → Replace image keeps its size and position.

Method 2: Build grid slides with an add-on

Photo Slides is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It inserts many photos from your computer into Google Slides at once, keeps them sharp (up to 3840 px, the most Google Slides keeps), and adds them as new slides at the end without touching your existing slides.

  1. Install Photo Slides from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Open your presentation and choose Extensions → Photo Slides: Bulk Photos to Google Slides → Insert photos.
  3. Click Pick photos or Pick a folder.
  4. Choose the order (file name, the order you picked, or date taken), the layout (1, 2, 4 or 6 photos per slide) and an optional caption (file name or date taken).
  5. Click Insert. To undo, click Remove the slides just added.

The free version inserts up to 20 photos at a time, one per slide, with no watermark. Grids of 2, 4 or 6, captions, sorting by date taken and no limit per run are in the paid version (a one-time $19). Details are on the Photo Slides product page.

Pitfalls

  • Mixed portrait and landscape photos do not fill a grid evenly. Crop them to the same shape, or choose "show the whole photo" and accept some white space.
  • Blurry photos: Google Slides stores images at up to 3840 px on the longest side. Photos inserted smaller than they will be shown look soft on a big screen.
  • Order: files named img2 and img10 can sort in the wrong order in some tools. Photo Slides sorts by number the way people expect (img2 before img10).

FAQ

Can I make a collage in Google Slides without an add-on? Yes, by hand with crop, Align and Distribute (Method 1). There is no automatic collage layout.

Can I put photos into a table in Google Slides? No. Table cells in Google Slides hold text, not images. Use Align and Distribute instead.

How many photos fit on one slide? For a projected slide, 4 is comfortable and 6 is the most that stays readable. More works for a contact-sheet style overview.

Google Slides is a trademark of Google LLC.

title: How to Print a Google Form as a Paper Quiz (With an Answer Key)
excerpt: Print a Google Form as a paper test: the built-in print, a free way to make an answer key, and how to get a worksheet layout with an answer key and A/B versions.
alt: A Google Form printed as a quiz, version A, version B and the answer key
content:
Short answer: Open the form in edit mode and choose More (⋮) → Print to print the blank form. It works, but questions can be split across pages, the layout follows the screen rather than a worksheet, and there is no answer key or A/B version. For a test you hand out in class, a print add-on such as Form Print (made by us) lays the questions out as a worksheet, keeps each question on one page, and prints an answer key and A/B versions.

Written: November 2026, Google Forms in Chrome.

Which situation are you in?

  • A quick paper copy, a few questions: the built-in print is enough (Method 1).
  • A paper test for a class, with an answer key: Method 2 for the key, or Method 3 for everything at once.
  • Printing what students already submitted: see Can You Print a Google Form? Blank, One Response, or All Responses.

Compare the ways

Way Questions kept on one page Answer key A/B versions Cost
Built-in print No No No Free
Submit the correct answers, print that response No Yes, as a filled form No Free
Form Print add-on (ours) Yes Yes, with points Yes Free up to 20 questions; paid $19 one-time

Method 1: Print the blank form

  1. Open the form in Google Forms (edit mode).
  2. Click More (⋮) at the top right → Print.
  3. In the print dialog, choose your printer, or Save as PDF as the destination.

Check the preview before printing a class set. Long questions, images and grids are often cut between two pages, and multiple-choice options keep their on-screen spacing, which wastes paper.

Method 2: Make an answer key from a response

  1. Open the form as a respondent (the Preview eye icon) and submit it once with the correct answers.
  2. Go to Responses → Individual, find your submission, and click the print icon.

This gives you a filled copy to check papers against. If the form is a quiz with points, the response view also shows the points. It is a workaround: the key has the same page breaks as the blank form, and the submission counts in your response data, so delete it afterwards if that matters.

Method 3: Print a worksheet, answer key and A/B versions (add-on)

Form Print for Google Forms is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It turns the form into a printable test or worksheet: multiple choice as circles, checkboxes as boxes, lines for written answers, grids as tables, and name, date and score fields at the top. No question is split across pages.

  1. Install Form Print from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Open the form, click the add-ons icon (puzzle piece) at the top, then Form Print for Google Forms → Open Form Print.
  3. Choose The blank form, the paper (A4 or Letter) and the options, then click Print / Save as PDF.
  4. For an answer key or A/B versions, turn them on before printing.

Form Print only reads the form you have open. It does not change the form or its responses and saves nothing to your Google Drive. The free version prints up to 20 questions per form with no watermark. The paid version (a one-time $19) removes the limit and adds two columns, the answer key with points and total, and A/B versions with shuffled questions and choices. The shuffle is the same every time for the same form, so the key always matches. All paid features are free for 7 days from the first time you open the add-on. Details are on the Form Print product page.

Pitfalls

  • Shuffle question order in the form's settings only affects the online form. It does not make printed versions.
  • Images in questions print at their on-screen size. Check that diagrams are big enough to read on paper.
  • Short answer lines: the built-in print gives one short line. If students need room to write, use a print layout with several answer lines.

FAQ

Can I print a Google Form quiz with the answers? Not from the blank-form print. Submit the correct answers once and print that response (Method 2), or print an answer key with an add-on (Method 3).

How do I stop questions splitting across pages? The built-in print has no setting for it. Shorter questions and fewer images help; a print add-on keeps each question together.

Can students fill in the printed form and I enter the scores later? Yes. Add a score field at the top, mark the papers, and type the results into a spreadsheet or the form.

Google Forms and Google Drive are trademarks of Google LLC.

title: How to Show Code in Google Slides for a Talk: Highlight Lines and Step Through
excerpt: Google Slides has no code block. Set up readable code slides, highlight the lines you are explaining, step through code, and split long code across slides.
alt: Codeglaze in Google Slides: a Python snippet in the One Dark theme with line numbers
content:
Short answer: Google Slides has no code block. For a talk, put the code in a text box with a monospace font and a dark fill, keep it to about 15 lines per slide, and point at the lines you are talking about with the highlight color button or by duplicating the slide and changing the highlight on each copy. An add-on such as Codeglaze (made by us) adds real syntax colors, line numbers, highlighted lines, and can split long code across slides or step through it.

Written: November 2026, Google Slides in Chrome.

What makes code readable on a projector

  • Size: 16 pt or larger. Below that, the back of the room cannot read it.
  • Length: about 12 to 15 lines per slide at that size. Split longer code.
  • Contrast: a dark background with light text, or the reverse. Avoid gray on gray.
  • Focus: show the whole snippet, then highlight the two or three lines you are explaining.

Compare the ways

Way Syntax colors Highlight lines Long code over several slides Cost
Text box by hand By hand By hand (highlight color) By hand Free
Screenshot of your editor Yes Only if your editor shows it By hand Free, but code cannot be copied
Codeglaze add-on (ours) Yes, 190+ languages Paid Paid, line numbers continue Free highlighting; paid $15 one-time

Method 1: Set up a code slide by hand

  1. Insert a text box (Insert → Text box) and paste the code.
  2. Set a monospace font such as Roboto Mono, Source Code Pro or Courier New, at 16 pt or more.
  3. With the text box selected, set a dark fill color and white or light text.
  4. To point at lines, select them and use the Highlight color button in the toolbar (the marker icon), or make them bold.

Method 2: Step through the code in your talk

With duplicated slides (works everywhere):

  1. Finish the code slide, then Slide → Duplicate slide once for each step.
  2. On each copy, highlight the next lines and remove the highlight from the previous ones.

When you click through, the code stays still and only the highlight moves, which is easy for the audience to follow.

With animation:

  1. Split the code into several text boxes stacked exactly on top of each other, or keep one box per block of lines.
  2. Select a box and choose Insert → Animation, then Appear, set to On click.

Animation reveals code a part at a time, but it is harder to keep the boxes lined up when you edit the code later. Duplicated slides are easier to maintain.

Method 3: Let an add-on color, number and step through the code

Codeglaze is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It adds real syntax highlighting to Google Slides and Google Docs: pick a language and one of 10 themes (VS Code, GitHub, Monokai, Dracula, One Dark, Nord and more), check the live preview, and insert the code as a box with a background.

  1. Install Codeglaze from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Select your code on the slide, or paste it into the panel.
  3. Open Extensions → Codeglaze → Open Codeglaze.
  4. Choose the language and theme, turn on line numbers if you want them, and click Insert.
  5. After editing the code, click Update to repaint the same box in place.

Highlighting is free, with no watermark or sign-up. The paid version (a one-time $15, free for 7 days) adds the features for talks: highlight lines (for example 3, 5-7), split long code over several slides with line numbers that continue, and step through code: the same code on several slides, highlighting the next lines on each one. It also adds diff colors (+ lines green, − lines red) and a window style with a file name header. Your code is highlighted in the side panel in your browser and is not sent to our servers. Details are on the Codeglaze product page.

Pitfalls

  • Presenting from another computer: fonts such as Roboto Mono and Source Code Pro come from Google Fonts and show on any computer. A font installed only on your laptop does not.
  • Exporting to PowerPoint: colored text and fills stay, but check the line spacing after export.
  • Screenshots of code look sharp on your screen but can blur when projected, and nobody can copy the code from the shared deck.

FAQ

How do I insert a code block in Google Slides? There is no code block feature. Use a text box with a monospace font and a fill color, or an add-on that inserts a highlighted code box.

Can I copy code from VS Code into Google Slides with the colors? Pasting from an editor sometimes keeps colors and sometimes does not, depending on the editor and browser. Check the result before relying on it.

What about Google Docs? Some Workspace editions have a built-in code block in Docs. See Syntax Highlighting in Google Docs and Slides: 4 Ways.

Google Slides and Google Docs are trademarks of Google LLC.

title: How to Sum a Column in a Google Docs Table (Docs Has No Formulas)
excerpt: Google Docs tables have no formulas. Three ways to get a column total: by hand, a linked table from Google Sheets, or an add-on that puts formulas and totals in the Docs table.
alt: Sumfit showing the before and after of a subtotal, tax and total in a Docs table
content:
Short answer: Google Docs tables have no formulas, so there is no built-in way to sum a column. You can add the numbers yourself, build the table in Google Sheets and paste it into Docs as a linked table that you update with one click, or use an add-on such as Sumfit (made by us) that puts the total right in your Docs table and recalculates it after you edit.

Written: November 2026, Google Docs in Chrome.

Which situation are you in?

  • A short table you will not change again: add it up by hand (Method 1).
  • The numbers already live in a spreadsheet, or the table is large: use a linked table from Google Sheets (Method 2).
  • The table belongs in the document (an invoice, a quote, a report) and you want totals that update: Method 3.

Compare the ways

Way Total stays correct after edits Table stays a normal Docs table Cost
Calculate by hand No, redo it yourself Yes Free
Linked table from Google Sheets Yes, after you click Update No, edit it in Sheets Free
Sumfit add-on (ours) Yes, after you click Recalculate Yes Free (up to 5 formulas per document); paid $19 one-time

Method 1: Add the numbers yourself

Copy the column into a calculator or a spreadsheet cell such as =SUM(...), then type the result into the total row. It is fine for a one-off, but the total goes stale as soon as someone changes a number.

Method 2: Paste a linked table from Google Sheets

  1. Put the table in Google Sheets and add the total with =SUM(B2:B9).
  2. Select the range, including the total row, and copy it.
  3. In Google Docs, paste. When asked, choose Link to spreadsheet.
  4. After the sheet changes, click Update on the table in Docs.

The total is always right, but you edit the numbers in Sheets, not in Docs, and anyone editing the document needs access to the spreadsheet to update it.

Method 3: Put totals and formulas in the Docs table (add-on)

Sumfit is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It adds sums, averages and simple formulas to tables in Google Docs. You see the result before anything changes, and Undo takes back the last change.

Sum a column:

  1. Install Sumfit from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Open your document and choose Extensions → Sumfit for Google Docs → Open Sumfit.
  3. Put the cursor in the empty cell where the total should go.
  4. Choose what to calculate (sum, average, count, max, min or multiply) of the cells above, to the left, or the cells you selected, and click Calculate.
  5. Check the before and after list, then click Put in. After editing numbers, click Recalculate.

Formulas in cells: type a formula that starts with = in a table cell, such as =B2*C2 or =SUM(D2:D9), open the Formulas tab and click Calculate formulas. Sumfit tells you when results are out of date and updates them with one button.

Sumfit reads currency symbols (¥ $ €), thousands separators, and negatives written as (100). The free version has formulas (SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, ROUND, IF and basic arithmetic) up to 5 per document, plus the column and row totals, with no watermark. The paid version (a one-time $19) removes the limits and adds SUMIF, weighted averages, references to other tables, an invoice and quote template with tax rows, sorting, charts and color rules. Details are on the Sumfit product page.

Pitfalls

  • Numbers stored as text with units ("12 pcs") are not read as numbers by most methods. Put units in the header instead.
  • Merged cells shift columns. Unmerge before calculating, or select the cells you want explicitly.
  • Pasted tables from other apps can carry hidden spaces. If a total looks wrong, check the cells it reads.

FAQ

Does Google Docs have a SUM formula for tables? No. Formulas work in Google Sheets, not in Docs tables. Use a linked Sheets table or an add-on.

Can I use =SUM in a Google Docs table? Typing it does nothing on its own. With Sumfit, =SUM(D2:D9) in a cell is calculated when you click Calculate formulas.

Will the total update automatically? Not by itself in any method. A linked table updates when you click Update; Sumfit updates when you click Recalculate.

Also in Sumfit: making many images the same size. See How to Resize All Images in Google Docs at Once.

Google Docs and Google Sheets are trademarks of Google LLC.

title: How to Change Icon Color in Google Slides (Recolor, Symbols and Add-ons)
excerpt: Icons inserted as pictures keep their color. How far Recolor goes, which symbols and shapes you can color freely, and how to pick or change the exact color with an add-on.
content:
Short answer: An icon you insert as a picture (PNG) keeps the color it was made in. Google Slides can only tint it with Format options → Recolor, which offers a few presets based on your theme colors. To get the exact color, insert the icon in that color in the first place (icon add-ons let you pick the color before inserting), use a symbol or shape whose color you can change, or use an add-on that can recolor icons you already placed, such as Icon Picker (made by us).

Written: November 2026, Google Slides in Chrome.

Which situation are you in?

  • Close enough is fine, and the color matches your theme: try Recolor (Method 1).
  • Simple symbols such as ✓, ★ or arrows: use special characters, which are text (Method 2).
  • Brand colors, or many icons that must match: pick the color before inserting, or recolor them all with an add-on (Method 3).

Compare the ways

Way Any color Recolor icons already on the slide Icon choice Cost
Format options → Recolor No, theme presets only Yes Any picture Free
Special characters or shapes Yes Yes Small set Free
Icon add-on that colors before inserting Depends on the add-on Usually no; insert again Large Varies
Icon Picker add-on (ours) Yes (paid: any color code) Yes (paid) 21,000+ icons Free 5 icons a day; paid $19 one-time

Method 1: Tint an icon with Recolor

  1. Click the icon on the slide.
  2. Click Format options in the toolbar (or right-click → Format options).
  3. Open Recolor and pick one of the presets.

The presets come from your theme's colors, as light and dark versions. For a one-color icon the result looks like a colored icon, but you cannot type a color code, and colored or detailed icons can look washed out.

Method 2: Use symbols or shapes you can color

  1. Click inside a text box and choose Insert → Special characters.
  2. Search for a symbol (for example "check", "star" or "arrow") and click it.
  3. Select the symbol and change the Text color like any other text.

Shapes from Insert → Shape work the same way with Fill color. Both stay sharp at any size, but the choice is small compared with an icon library.

Method 3: Choose the color in an icon add-on

Icon Picker is an add-on made by us, Daily Picks. It searches more than 21,000 icons (Material Symbols, Tabler, Lucide, Phosphor and Heroicons) and inserts them into Google Slides and Google Docs as sharp PNG images in the color and size you choose. The icons are built into the add-on, so nothing is downloaded from outside and your file is not sent anywhere.

  1. Install Icon Picker from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Choose Extensions → Icon Picker: Icons for Google Slides & Docs → Open Icon Picker.
  3. Search for an icon, pick a color and size, and click Insert.

Change the color of icons you already inserted (paid): select the icons, or choose this slide or all slides, pick the new color, and Icon Picker replaces them in place. The position and size stay the same. You can also use your theme's colors with one click, so icons match the rest of the deck.

The free version gives 5 icons a day from Material Symbols (about 7,800 icons) in a 12-color palette, with no watermark. The paid version (a one-time $19) has no daily limit and adds every icon set, any color code, up to 2048 px, icons on a circle or square background, and recoloring icons already in the file. Details are on the Icon Picker product page.

Pitfalls

  • Icons downloaded from websites as PNG have their color baked in. Recolor tints them but cannot give an exact brand color.
  • Low-resolution icons look blurry when enlarged. Insert them at the size you will show them, or larger.
  • Icon licenses: check the license of icons from websites. The sets in Icon Picker are open source (Apache-2.0, MIT and ISC), and the license texts are in the sidebar.

FAQ

Why can't I change the fill color of an icon in Google Slides? Because it is a picture, not a shape. Fill color works on shapes; pictures can only be recolored with the presets.

Can I insert SVG icons and color them? Google Slides does not keep inserted icons as editable vector shapes; they become pictures. Pick the color before inserting.

How do I make all icons on my slides the same color? Insert them with the same color from the start, or use an add-on that recolors every inserted icon at once.

For icons in Google Docs, see How to Insert Icons in Google Docs (4 Free Ways).

Google Slides and Google Docs are trademarks of Google LLC.
